wu: Warm-up: 'Simon Says' with classroom objects. Teacher says 'Simon says touch your pencil' or 'Simon says show me your book'. Students touch or show the object. If they move without 'Simon says', they sit down. Teacher asks 'What is it?' and students say 'It is a pencil/book'.
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: 'Mystery Bag'. Teacher puts a classroom object in a bag. Students feel it and guess 'Is it a pen?'. Teacher says 'Yes, it is' or 'No, it isn't'.
Alternative warm-up 2: 'Flashcard Race'. Two lines of students. Teacher shows a flashcard. First student to say the word (e.g., 'bag') gets a point for their team.
pres: Presentation: Teacher uses real classroom objects (pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table). Holds up each object and says 'This is a pen.' Students repeat. Then models the question 'Can I have the pen, please?' and gives the object to a student. Students practice asking and receiving.
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: 'Story Time'. Teacher tells a short story about a character who needs classroom objects. 'Ali needs a pen. Can I have the pen, please?' Students repeat the requests.
Alternative presentation 2: 'Flashcard Dialogue'. Teacher shows flashcards of objects and models the dialogue: 'What is it?' 'It is a book.' 'Can I have the book, please?'
prac: Guided practice: 'Pass the Object'. Students sit in a circle. Teacher gives an object to one student and says 'Can I have the pencil, please?'. The student passes it to the next student, who must say the full request. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: 'Find the Object'. Teacher says 'Can I have the book, please?'. Students point to the book on their desks. First to point correctly gets a sticker.
Alternative practice 2: 'Pair Dialogue'. Students work in pairs. Student A holds an object. Student B says 'Can I have the __, please?'. Student A gives it and says 'Here you are.'
ls: Listening slot: 'Listen and Draw'. Teacher describes a scene: 'Draw a table. On the table, draw a book and a pen. Next to the table, draw a chair.' Students follow instructions and draw. Teacher checks drawings to confirm comprehension of object names and prepositions.
re: Reactivation game: 'Musical Objects'. Play music. Students walk around the classroom. When music stops, teacher calls out an object (e.g., 'bag!'). Students must find and touch a bag. Last one to touch is 'out' but becomes the next caller.
prod: Production task: 'Classroom Shop'. Set up a 'shop' with classroom objects. Students take turns being the shopkeeper and customers. Customers must say 'Can I have the __, please?' to request an object. Shopkeeper says 'Here you are.' Students use 'this/that' (e.g., 'Can I have that pen, please?').
rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Label and Trace'. Students look at a worksheet with pictures of classroom objects but no words. They trace the words 'pen', 'pencil', 'book', 'bag', 'chair', 'table' below the pictures. Then, they copy the words into their notebooks next to the correct picture.
st: Story / song + goodbye: Read 'The Day I Lost My Pencil' story, focusing on repeated object words. Sing the 'Hello Goodbye Song'. End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teacher calls out object words. Students cover the matching picture on their bingo card. First to get a line shouts 'Bingo!'
Teacher places 3 objects on a table. Students close eyes. Teacher removes one. Students open eyes and say 'The pen is missing! Can I have the pen, please?'
Two teams race to bring a requested object to the teacher. Teacher says 'Can I have the book, please?'. First student to bring the book gets a point.
Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something beginning with b'. Students guess 'Is it a book?'. Teacher says 'Yes, it is.'
Students match flashcards of objects to word cards on the board. Say the word aloud when making a match.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a short sentence about their favourite classroom object and draw a picture of it using 'This is my __.'
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with picture clues to label the objects on their worksheet.
hw: Homework option 1: Draw a picture of your desk and label 3 objects (e.g., 'This is my book.')
Homework option 2: Ask your family for objects using 'Can I have the __, please?' and write down what they said
Homework option 3: Make flashcards for 6 classroom objects and practice saying the words with a family member
tip: Use the local context of American Space Oujda by connecting the lesson to 'What objects do you use in the library?' to reinforce real-world use of the language.
